issues.description: Inconsistent specification of the Animal.name attribute type: the UML in the problem statement declares the attribute as 'name: String' while the textual instruction explicitly tells students to use StringBuilder for the name (problem_statement.md). The provided solution implements the field as a String (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java) and the template Main (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java) instantiates animals using String constructor arguments. This mismatch (UML vs. textual instruction vs. solution/template) will confuse students about which type to use and which constructor signature to implement; following the textual instruction (StringBuilder) could make their classes incompatible with the given examples and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and examples consistent. Either: (A) Change the textual instruction to require a String (so UML, examples, and solution align), or (B) change the UML to 'StringBuilder' and update the solution and template to use a StringBuilder field (and ensure constructors accept a compatible type or convert String parameters into a StringBuilder). A practical approach: require constructors to accept String (as shown in Main) but store the value internally in a StringBuilder (e.g., this.name = new StringBuilder(name)), and update the problem text to clarify this expected constructor behavior.
